title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two project management tools used by software development teams to track and manage their work. This comparison is useful for teams considering switching from Jira to Plane, possibly due to the core use case of issue tracking and project management, and the key reason being the desire for more control over their data and costs. Teams looking for a self-hosted solution with more flexibility may benefit from this comparison.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira is a paid tool with a per-user monthly fee, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows teams to have full control over their data, while Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Jira has a more complex setup process, while Plane is relatively simpler to set up.
* Scalability: Jira is designed to handle large teams and projects, while Plane may require more configuration to scale.
* Integration with Git: Jira has native integration with Git, while Plane uses third-party integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550-$2,900/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Jira
* Pros:
  + Scalable and reliable
  + Native integration with Git
  + Large community of users and developers
  + Wide range of features and customization options
  + Good customer support
* Cons:
  + Expensive, especially for large teams
  + Complex setup process
  + Limited control over data
  + Proprietary license
### Plane
* Pros:
  + Free and self-hosted
  + Full control over data
  + Simple setup process
  + Customizable and extensible
  + Apache 2.0 license
* Cons:
  + Limited scalability out of the box
  + No native integration with Git
  + Limited customer support
  + May require more configuration to set up

## When to Choose Each
Jira is a good choice for large teams with complex project management needs, who require a scalable and reliable solution with native integration with Git. Plane is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams who want a self-hosted solution with full control over their data, and are willing to configure and customize the tool to meet their needs.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Jira in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Plane instance on your server.
3. Use the Plane import tool to import your data from the CSV or JSON file.
4. Configure and customize Plane to meet your team's needs.
5. Test and verify that all data has been imported correctly.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some features and polish. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Plane's scalability is limited out of the box, and may require additional configuration to handle large teams or projects. However, for small to medium-sized teams who want a self-hosted solution with full control over their data, Plane is a good choice, and we recommend considering it as an alternative to Jira.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who don't need native Git integration
* Teams who want full control over their data and are willing to self-host
* Teams with simple project management needs who don't require a lot of customization
* Teams who are currently using Jira and are looking to reduce costs
* Teams who value the flexibility and customizability of an open-source solution

## FAQ
### Is Plane free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted. You only need to pay for the server costs.
### Does Plane have native integration with Git?
No, Plane uses third-party integrations to connect with Git.
### Can I export my data from Jira and import it into Plane?
Yes, you can export your data from Jira in CSV or JSON format and import it into Plane using the import tool.
### Is Plane scalable?
Plane's scalability is limited out of the box, and may require additional configuration to handle large teams or projects.
### Does Plane have good customer support?
No, Plane's customer support is limited, as it is an open-source solution.
meta_description: Plane, a free self-hosted project management tool, offers more control over data. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan

## Overview

Trello is a visual kanban board tool from Atlassian, simple and beginner-friendly. WeKan is an open-source kanban board offering the same card/list/board model without vendor dependency.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Trello paid plans start at $5/user/month; WeKan is completely free
- **Data control**: WeKan runs on your own server; Trello data lives on Atlassian infrastructure
- **Features**: Trello has a larger Power-Ups marketplace; WeKan covers core kanban features
- **Setup**: Trello requires zero setup; WeKan requires a server
- **Customization**: WeKan open-source code can be extended; Trello cannot

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Trello

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### WeKan

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [wekan/wekan](https://github.com/wekan/wekan) * ~20k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Trello if:** Trello suits individuals and small teams wanting instant zero-setup kanban with integrations to Slack, Google Drive, and GitHub.

**Choose WeKan if:** WeKan is ideal for teams wanting full data ownership or air-gapped deployments.

## Migration Path

Export Trello boards as JSON, then use WeKan Trello importer in Settings to recreate boards, lists, and cards.

## Our Take

WeKan is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Trello tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your WeKan instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Trello, switching to self-hosted WeKan will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Trello until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Trello paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is WeKan free to use?
Yes. WeKan is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Trello to WeKan?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Trello data, follow the WeKan import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does WeKan get regular updates?
Yes. WeKan has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use WeKan without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if WeKan development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Trello](https://trello.com) and [WeKan](https://wekan.github.io) before making decisions.*

# Dropbox vs Nextcloud (2026)

## Overview
Dropbox and Nextcloud are cloud storage solutions that allow users to store and share files. This comparison is useful for individuals and teams who are looking for a reliable and secure way to manage their files, and are considering switching from Dropbox to Nextcloud due to concerns about data ownership and cost. The core use case for both tools is file storage and sharing, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Dropbox charges a monthly fee per user, while Nextcloud is free to use with self-hosting.
* Data ownership: Nextcloud allows users to retain full ownership of their data, while Dropbox's terms of service grant the company certain rights to user data.
* Setup complexity: Nextcloud requires more technical expertise to set up and configure, while Dropbox is generally easier to use out of the box.
* Scalability: Nextcloud is highly scalable and can be easily integrated with existing infrastructure, while Dropbox has limitations on the amount of storage and bandwidth available to users.
* Integration with other tools: Nextcloud has a built-in integration with OnlyOffice for document editing, while Dropbox has a similar integration with Microsoft Office Online.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Dropbox | Nextcloud |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $9.99-$16.58/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $499.50-$829/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,998-$3,316/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Dropbox:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Integrates well with other tools and services
* Has a large user base and community
* Offers a free version with limited storage
* Has a user-friendly interface
* Limited control over data and security
* Can be expensive for large teams or organizations
* Has limitations on storage and bandwidth
* Does not offer self-hosting options
**Nextcloud:**
* Offers self-hosting options for full control over data
* Is highly scalable and customizable
* Has a large community of developers and users
* Offers a wide range of integrations with other tools and services
* Is free to use with self-hosting
* Can be complex to set up and configure
* Requires technical expertise to manage and maintain
* Can be resource-intensive and require significant server resources

## When to Choose Each
When to choose Dropbox: Dropbox is a good choice for small teams or individuals who need a simple and easy-to-use cloud storage solution. It is also a good choice for those who are already invested in the Dropbox ecosystem and have a large number of files and folders stored on the platform. However, for larger teams or organizations that require more control over their data and security, Nextcloud may be a better option.
When to choose Nextcloud: Nextcloud is a good choice for larger teams or organizations that require more control over their data and security. It is also a good choice for those who are looking for a highly scalable and customizable cloud storage solution. Additionally, Nextcloud is a good choice for those who are concerned about data ownership and want to retain full control over their files and folders.

## Migration Path
1. Export your files and folders from Dropbox using the Dropbox API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up a Nextcloud server and configure it to meet your needs.
3. Import your files and folders into Nextcloud using the Nextcloud API or a third-party tool.
4. Configure any necessary integrations with other tools and services.
5. Test your Nextcloud setup to ensure that it is working as expected.

## Our Take
Nextcloud is a highly capable and customizable cloud storage solution that offers a wide range of features and integrations. However, it may not be the best choice for all users, particularly those who are not technically inclined or who require a high level of support and maintenance. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Nextcloud can be resource-intensive and require significant server resources, particularly if you have a large number of users or files.
Nextcloud is a complex system that requires significant technical expertise to set up and manage. While it is highly customizable and scalable, it may not be the best choice for small teams or individuals who are looking for a simple and easy-to-use cloud storage solution.
We recommend switching to Nextcloud if you are a larger team or organization that requires more control over your data and security, and are willing and able to invest the time and resources necessary to set up and manage the system. However, if you are a small team or individual who is looking for a simple and easy-to-use cloud storage solution, Dropbox may be a better choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Large teams or organizations with more than 50 users who require more control over their data and security
* Teams or individuals who are concerned about data ownership and want to retain full control over their files and folders
* Developers or IT professionals who are looking for a highly customizable and scalable cloud storage solution
* Teams or individuals who require a high level of integration with other tools and services
* Educational institutions or non-profit organizations that are looking for a free or low-cost cloud storage solution

## FAQ
### What is the difference between Dropbox and Nextcloud?
Nextcloud is a self-hosted cloud storage solution that offers more control over data and security, while Dropbox is a proprietary cloud storage solution that is easier to use but offers less control.
### Can I use Nextcloud for free?
Yes, Nextcloud is free to use with self-hosting, although you will need to pay for server costs and maintenance.
### Is Nextcloud secure?
Yes, Nextcloud is highly secure and offers a wide range of security features, including encryption and two-factor authentication.
### Can I integrate Nextcloud with other tools and services?
Yes, Nextcloud offers a wide range of integrations with other tools and services, including OnlyOffice and Microsoft Office Online.
### Is Nextcloud easy to use?
No, Nextcloud can be complex to set up and configure, particularly for those who are not technically inclined.

- **License**: Google Workspace is Proprietary; Nextcloud is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Nextcloud can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Nextcloud eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Nextcloud has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Google Workspace | Nextcloud |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $6-$18/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$300/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,200/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Google Workspace

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Nextcloud

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [nextcloud/server](https://github.com/nextcloud/server) * ~27k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Google Workspace if:** Google Workspace is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Nextcloud if:** Nextcloud is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Google Workspace in its standard export format, review Nextcloud import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Nextcloud is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Google Workspace tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Nextcloud instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Google Workspace, switching to self-hosted Nextcloud will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Google Workspace until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Google Workspace paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Nextcloud free to use?
Yes. Nextcloud is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Google Workspace to Nextcloud?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Google Workspace data, follow the Nextcloud import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Nextcloud get regular updates?
Yes. Nextcloud has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Nextcloud without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Nextcloud development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com) and [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) before making decisions.*
